title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Refer adults with persistent synovitis of undetermined cause to a specialist, and refer urgently if the small joints of the hands or feet are affected.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Refer urgently, even with a normal acute-phase response, if more than one joint is affected or there has been a delay of three months or longer between symptom onset and seeking advice.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Do not avoid referring urgently because blood tests show a normal acute-phase response or negative antibodies.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Offer to carry out a blood test for rheumatoid factor in adults with suspected inflammatory joint disease who are found to have synovitis on clinical examination.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Consider measuring anti-CCP antibodies in adults with suspected inflammatory joint disease if they are negative for rheumatoid factor.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: X-ray the hands and feet early in the course of the disease in adults with persistent synovitis.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Offer first-line treatment with a conventional disease-modifying drug as monotherapy as soon as possible and ideally within three months of onset of persistent symptoms.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Consider short-term bridging treatment with glucocorticoids when starting a new disease-modifying drug.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Escalate dose as tolerated and consider a second disease-modifying drug in combination when the treatment target has not been reached.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Measure disease activity with a validated composite score at each review until the treatment target is reached, then monitor monthly.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Offer an annual review that assesses disease activity, damage, comorbidities and the need for referral to other services.

title: Fictional inflammatory joint disease: assessment and management
text: Offer short-term glucocorticoids for managing flares to rapidly decrease inflammation, and do not use them long term unless other options have been offered.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: Consider a back-up antibiotic prescription or an immediate antibiotic prescription for women with lower urinary tract infection who are not pregnant.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: Give advice about managing symptoms with self-care, including drinking enough fluids and taking paracetamol for pain.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: Offer an immediate antibiotic prescription to men and to pregnant women with lower urinary tract infection, taking account of the severity of symptoms.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: Advise people to seek medical help if symptoms worsen rapidly, do not start to improve within 48 hours of taking the antibiotic, or the person becomes systemically very unwell.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: When prescribing for a non-pregnant woman, choose a three-day course of the first-line agent, and follow the local formulary where resistance is known.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: When prescribing for a man, choose a seven-day course and review the diagnosis if symptoms do not settle.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: Send a urine sample for culture before starting treatment in pregnant women, men, and people whose symptoms have recurred within six months.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: Reassess if symptoms worsen at any time or do not improve within 48 hours, taking account of other possible diagnoses and any symptoms of a more serious illness.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: Refer people to hospital if they have symptoms or signs suggesting a more serious illness or condition such as sepsis.

title: Fictional lower urinary tract infection in adults: antimicrobial prescribing
text: Consider referral or specialist advice for people with recurrent lower urinary tract infection, defined as two episodes in six months or three in a year.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Consider using a headache diary to aid the diagnosis of primary headaches, recording frequency, duration, severity and associated symptoms for a minimum of eight weeks.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Do not refer people diagnosed with tension-type headache, migraine or cluster headache for neuroimaging solely for reassurance.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Refer urgently people who present with headache and new onset neurological deficit, a change in personality, or a headache triggered by cough, exercise or posture.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Consider aspirin, paracetamol or a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug for the acute treatment of tension-type headache, taking into account the person's preference and comorbidities.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Do not offer opioids for the acute treatment of tension-type headache.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Offer combination therapy with an oral triptan and a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug, or an oral triptan and paracetamol, for the acute treatment of migraine.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Offer a preventive medicine to people with migraine after discussing the benefits and risks, when attacks are frequent or disabling.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Advise people with migraine that riboflavin at a daily dose may be effective in reducing frequency and intensity for some people.

title: Fictional headache in adults: diagnosis and management
text: Be alert to the possibility of medication overuse headache in people whose headache developed or worsened while taking acute treatments on ten or more days a month.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Consider assessment of fracture risk in all women aged 65 and over and all men aged 75 and over.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Consider assessment of fracture risk in younger adults in the presence of risk factors such as previous fragility fracture, current or frequent use of oral glucocorticoids, or a history of falls.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Do not routinely assess fracture risk in people aged under 50 years unless they have major risk factors.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Estimate absolute risk when assessing risk of fracture, using a validated tool, and recognise that the tools may underestimate risk in people taking high-dose glucocorticoids.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Do not routinely measure bone mineral density to assess fracture risk without prior assessment using a validated tool.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Consider measuring bone mineral density before starting treatments that may have a rapid adverse effect on bone density.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Consider recalculating fracture risk if the original calculated risk was close to the intervention threshold and after a minimum of two years.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Reassess fracture risk when there has been a change in the person's risk factors, such as a new fragility fracture or starting long-term glucocorticoids.

title: Fictional bone fragility: assessing the risk of fracture
text: Offer treatment for bone protection to people starting long-term oral glucocorticoids at a high dose without waiting for a fracture risk assessment.
